record.paper_title: Infinity in string cosmology: A review through open problems
record.original_question: Are the cosmological solutions in M-theory that are associated with a BPS state stable under the inhomogeneous perturbations required by such solutions, and how does that stability affect their possible role in the ambient cosmological construction?

evidence.quote:
2.5 Asymptotics of M-theory cosmology II
This is an extension of the previous problem in a diﬀerent direction. The plan is to examine the stability of those cosmological solutions that are associated with a BPS state cf. [50]. This requires the solutions to be inhomogeneous, and so may also have a signiﬁcant role to play in the ambient cosmological construction.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider eleven-dimensional supergravity (the low-energy limit of M-theory), whose bosonic field content consists of a Lorentzian metric g and a 3-form gauge potential A with 4-form field strength F = dA, governed by the action S = (1/2κ²)∫(R*1 − ½ F∧*F − (1/6) A∧F∧F). A cosmological solution of this theory is a solution (g, A) on a spacetime of the form M = R_t × X (with X a spatial slice) in which the metric and fluxes depend non-trivially on the time coordinate. Such a solution is said to be associated with a BPS state if it preserves a non-zero fraction of the supersymmetries of the theory, i.e. it admits at least one Killing spinor ε satisfying the gravitino variation equation δψ_μ = ∇_μ ε + (1/288)(Γ_μ^{νρσλ} − 8 δ_μ^ν Γ^{ρσλ}) F_{νρσλ} ε = 0. Because BPS-preserving cosmological backgrounds in this setting are generically not spatially homogeneous, perturbations around them must in general be taken to be inhomogeneous (i.e. depending on the spatial coordinates on X as well as on t).

Problem: Determine whether every cosmological solution of eleven-dimensional supergravity that is associated with (i.e. preserves some supersymmetry of) a BPS state is linearly stable under inhomogeneous perturbations of the metric and 4-form field strength. More precisely, for each such background (g, A), study the linearized equations of motion for perturbations (δg, δA) that depend non-trivially on the spatial coordinates, and decide whether all physical modes remain bounded (in a suitable energy norm) as t evolves toward the asymptotic regimes of the solution. Furthermore, analyse how the presence or absence of such stability constrains the role of these BPS cosmological backgrounds within a larger (possibly non-supersymmetric) cosmological construction in which they appear as building blocks or asymptotic regions.
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not surface a definitive resolution of the stability of BPS-associated cosmological solutions in M-theory under inhomogeneous perturbations. The available literature addresses cosmological perturbation theory and stability in modified gravity, but does not provide a general stability theorem for BPS cosmological backgrounds in eleven-dimensional supergravity. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Inhomogeneous Perturbations and Stability Analysis of the Einstein Static Universe in f(R,T) Gravity
status_evidence.snippet: Inhomogeneous linear perturbations are used to study stability in modified gravity, but not for M-theory BPS cosmological backgrounds.
status_evidence.claim: General techniques exist for inhomogeneous perturbation stability, but no direct resolution for BPS M-theory cosmologies is found.

status_evidence.title: Cosmological perturbation theory - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Cosmological perturbation theory is the theory by which the evolution of structure is understood in the Big Bang model.
status_evidence.claim: Standard cosmological perturbation theory does not specifically address BPS M-theory backgrounds.
